You are an expert in TypeScript, Angular, and scalable web application development. You write functional, maintainable, performant, and accessible code following Angular and TypeScript best practices.

## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict type checking
- Prefer type inference when the type is obvious
- Avoid the `any` type; use `unknown` when type is uncertain

- Always use angular schematics for new files (ng generate ...) unless there is no generator
  - Do not change options - schematic will use angular.json defaults
  - For pages use `ng g c ... --type=page`
  - For models use `ng g interface ...`
  - For data sources and services use `ng g s ...`

- Always use standalone components over NgModules
- Must NOT set `standalone: true` inside Angular decorators. It's the default in Angular v20+.
- Do NOT set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` explicitly. `OnPush` is the default in Angular v22+.
- Use signals for state management
- Implement lazy loading for feature routes
- Do NOT use the `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators. Put host bindings inside the `host` object of the `@Component` or `@Directive` decorator instead
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for all static images.
  - `NgOptimizedImage` does not work for inline base64 images.

## Accessibility Requirements

- It MUST pass all AXE checks.
- It MUST follow all WCAG AA minimums, including focus management, color contrast, and ARIA attributes.

## Components

- Keep components small and focused on a single responsibility
- Use `input()` and `output()` functions instead of decorators
- Use `model()` for two-way bound properties with `[(prop)]` syntax instead of pairing `input()` with `output()`
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Use `linkedSignal()` for state derived from multiple reactive sources that must stay synchronized
- Prefer inline templates for small components
- Prefer Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) for new forms. They are stable in Angul

_**Agent (copilot/claude-haiku-5.5)**_

Here's a simple approach using content projection. The parent is a layout wrapper, and the child is a label + projected value. No shared state is needed for this.

**1. Generate both components** (per the project's schematic rule, under the shared UI folder since nothing here is deal-specific):

```sh
ng g c shared/ui/info-grid
ng g c shared/ui/info-item
```

**2. Parent: layout only**

```ts
// shared/ui/info-grid/info-grid.ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-info-grid',
  host: { class: 'mt-5 grid grid-cols-3 gap-4' },
  template: `<ng-content />`,
})
export class InfoGrid {}
```

**3. Child: label + projected value**

```ts
// shared/ui/info-item/info-item.ts
import { Component, input } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-info-item',
  template: `
    <span class="text-label-lg text-on-surface">{{ label() }}</span>
    <div class="mt-1 text-body-lg text-on-surface">
      <ng-content />
    </div>
  `,
})
export class InfoItem {
  label = input.required<string>();
}
```

**4. Usage in `src/app/features/deals/ui/deal-details-card/deal-details-card.ts`**

```html
<app-info-grid>
  <app-info-item label="Value">$48,000</app-info-item>
  <app-info-item label="Contact">Anna Kowalska</app-info-item>
  <app-info-item label="Public">{{ deal.public ? 'Yes' : 'No' }}</app-info-item>
</app-info-grid>
```

The `deal` alias from `@if` is still in scope, so the projected content can read it. If you need a different value style (for example `text-title-md` for the value), add a small input to the child rather than duplicating the component.

**Caveat:** The original uses `<dl>/<div>/<dt>/<dd>`, which is the more semantic markup. Custom elements inside `<dl>` are invalid HTML. If you want to keep that semantics, use an attribute selector on real elements (`dl[appInfoGrid]`, `div[appInfoItem]`) instead of custom element tags. The version above trades that for simplicity.

**Naming ideas**

Parent (layout role):
- `InfoGrid` / `app-info-grid`: my pick, describes the layout
- `DetailsGrid` / `app-details-grid`
- `FactGrid` / `app-fact-grid`
- `DescriptionList` / `app-description-list`: matches `<dl>` semantics if you keep it

Child (label + value pair):
- `InfoItem` / `app-info-item`: my pick, pairs with `InfoGrid`
- `DetailItem` / `app-detail-item`
- `Fact` / `app-fact`: short and clear for label/value pairs
- `DescriptionItem` / `app-description-item`: pairs with `DescriptionList`

Avoid a `Deal` prefix if the component should be reused across Contacts and Tasks. Pick one pair and keep both names in the same family.

Do you want me to create these files and update `deal-details-card.ts`?

          <app-info-item label="Value" [value]="deal.value | currency" />

          <app-info-item label="Public">{{ deal.public ? 'Yes' : 'No' }}</app-info-item>
        </app-info-grid>
      </article>
    } @else {
      <div class="px-3 py-4 text-center">No deal selected</div>
    }
  `,
})
export class DealDetailsCard {
  deal = input<Deal>();

  onEdit() {

}

import { Component, input } from '@angular/core';

/**
 * Label/value pair. The `label` input or a `[info-label]` element renders the label; the `value` input or projected content renders the value.
 *
 * @example
 * ```html
 * <app-info-item label="Value" value="$48,000" />
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```html
 * <app-info-item value="Anna Kowalska">
 *   <span info-label>Contact</span>
 * </app-info-item>
 * ```
 *
 * @example
 * ```html
 * <app-info-item label="Public">{{ deal.public ? 'Yes' : 'No' }}</app-info-item>
 * ```
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-info-item',
  template: `
    <div class="text-label-lg text-on-surface">
      <ng-content select="[info-label]">{{ label() }}</ng-content>
    </div>
    <div class="mt-1 text-body-lg text-on-surface">
      <ng-content>{{ value() }}</ng-content>
    </div>
  `,
})
export class InfoItem {
  label = input<string | null>();
  value = input<string | null>();
}
````
</details></tool-use>
